# agentglass

> The workspace for your coding agents. One window on a developer's own machine holds the terminals (real tmux panes), the agents — Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode — their pull requests and reviews, the diffs they write, git and Docker, a browser they can drive, and every approval they are waiting on, so nobody has to switch to another app. Local by default: a Bun + SQLite server on loopback, a desktop app (Linux, macOS, Windows) and an Android companion. Open source, MIT.

It attaches to agents already running in tmux and in the repositories already open, and it can start them too: a task cuts a worktree and seats an agent in it with the prompt written. It reads them through their own hook and transcript streams, holds the tool calls a person chose to gate until somebody says go, and gives the agents a browser of their own — one already signed in to what the person is signed in to — driven from a CLI and an MCP server.

- [Configuration and API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SirAllap/agentglass/main/docs/CONFIG.md): every environment variable the code reads, the whole HTTP API, the architecture
- [Security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SirAllap/agentglass/main/SECURITY.md): the trust model, what each surface can reach, retention, how to report a vulnerability
- [Extending](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SirAllap/agentglass/main/docs/EXTENDING.md): driving agentglass from your own harness, and writing a plugin
- [Plugins](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SirAllap/agentglass/main/docs/PLUGINS.md): what a plugin is, what it may ask for, how to publish one
- [Changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SirAllap/agentglass/main/CHANGELOG.md): what each release changed
